rows.48:0bb4:
You didn't see it?
Come on, you don't have to lie to me of all people.{p}
rows.48:21e0:
On a day off, I hid by the window in my house and watched her house all day long.
The guy showed up early in the morning, and he took so long to come out of the house that I started getting mad, wondering when he'd ever leave.{p}
rows.48:22c0:
I got sleepy, too.
I was only in junior high, after all.
By the time I rubbed my drowsy eyes and looked at the clock with my head all foggy, it was already past midnight.
That was way too late, any way you look at it.
I was just thinking, how could her parents put up with this, when he finally came out.{p}
rows.48:28c0:
That day, it wasn't even evening yet.
But even so, that guy came bursting out of the house.{p}
rows.48:2910:
And right behind him, Shimizu came out, wailing and sobbing.
When people say someone's hair is flying wild and they're crying with their whole face, I guess that's the kind of face they mean.
And she was throwing the books and paints and stuff in her hands at him.
The guy was just smirking.
Smirking like he was making fun of Shimizu.{p}
rows.48:2b78:
"Don't think I can't do it! Scum like you, I'll kill you!"
That was the first time I'd ever seen her look so terrifying.
She really looked like she'd kill him any second.
Even so, the guy just sneered and started wobbling off again.
She collapsed right there in tears.{p}
rows.48:2cc0:
About a month after that, she was murdered.
Somebody strangled her.
In fact, when she was killed, the police came around asking questions at my house and all over the neighborhood.
I kept my mouth shut, but somebody must've talked, don't you think?
About that guy.
It was that big of a fight, after all.
It wouldn't be strange if everybody remembered it.
Or if they'd told the cops about it, too.{p}
rows.48:3ad4: Even so, she must have kept coming back as a ghost day after day, finishing the painting little by little, trying to seal the man inside it.{p}
rows.48:414c:
{f:I|I} watched Shindo leave.
I'd forgotten, and that was that{f:.|.}{p}
rows.48:6bc0:
What do you think was inside...?
Thin, tightly rolled-up things, kind of like paper.
There were tons and tons of them in there.
I figured they had to be the stuff you paint on... canvas, right? That stuff.
I knew she painted, after all.
But the stench seemed to be coming from those canvases.
I nervously reached out.
The instant I touched one, I knew what it was.
It wasn't cloth.
And it definitely wasn't paper.
It was the skin of something.
That's where the stench was coming from.{p}
rows.48:700c:
Her face right then was just like a witch's.
I got scared and shoved her as hard as I could.
And while she was off balance, I bolted out of the room.
Even after I'd run all the way home, my heart kept pounding for a good while.
Was that who she really was?
Behind all that kindness, had she been waiting for her chance to skin me?
Thinking about it scared me so bad that for a while I had nightmares.
We never got together again after that.
I kept away from her, and whenever we ran into each other on the street, she'd ignore me.{p}
rows.48:8414:
What I saw there... was her, sitting facing a painting.
That alone was nothing unusual.
But something about her was different.
She had her lips pursed, like she was sucking something in.
No, she really was sucking it in.
When I strained my eyes, I could see something sparkly, like light or powder, flowing from the painting into her mouth.
After a while, she let out a satisfied sigh.
"...I'll have to paint over it again."
I heard her say that.
What did that mean?{p}
rows.48:89d4:
Maybe the painting's life force was her source of energy.
The life force of the person in the painting, that is.
I don't know why a painting of anyone else wouldn't do, but I bet her narcissism was the key.
So I think she tried to finish her self-portrait so she could soak up plenty of life force.
Maybe if she had, she could've come back to life.{p}
